correctness.rationale: With distinct first t−1 draws, the prefix must contain i once and the last draw must equal i. Ordering each such prefix gives the (t−1)! factor and p_i² times e_{t−2} on the other labels. Remove i and j and write a_s=e_s of the remaining masses. Comparing conditional odds at t and t+1 cancels all common factors; the earlier-minus-later cross-product is (p_i−p_j)(a_s²−a_{s−1}a_{s+1}) for s=t−2. The positive endpoint cells and zero conventions give strictness at both ends, including m=2; strict unnormalized Newton log-concavity gives interior strictness from the normalized inequality and the strict binomial factor. Denominators are positive and equal masses give constant odds. For a nonuniform vector the successive conditional likelihood ratio is strictly decreasing across distinct mass values; taking its covariance with g under the earlier law gives a strictly negative change of the conditional g-mean. Taking covariance of that decreasing mean with f(T) proves the strict inequality, since T has full support. The endpoint laws follow by taking e_0 and the product of all complementary masses. Equality of those laws forces uniformity; conversely uniformity gives exchangeability and independence. I inspected the exact finite checker without running it; the argument covers all times and label pairs independently of the finite tests.

evidence: Camarri–Pitman give P(A_1=A)=|A|! (product of the masses in A)(sum of the masses in A). Flajolet–Gardy–Thimonier give unmarked waiting-time expectations in symmetric functions. Fadnavis gives fixed-draw noncollision probabilities and compares the effect of changing the probability vector.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Marking the final draw with i replaces the summed mass by p_i and summing over admissible sets recovers the joint law. An unmarked or set-valued probability, and a fixed-time comparison over different vectors, do not by themselves supply a stated comparison of label odds over times for one vector. The earlier equivalent record, not these background formulas or an unavailable paper, decides the verdict.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Strict adjacent MLR makes the mean of every strictly increasing g of the mass strictly decrease by the finite-support covariance identity. Taking covariance with any strictly increasing f(T) gives the additional covariance clause. Independence would equate the two endpoint laws, which by p_i>0 forces every mass to equal the same sum of squares; exchangeability gives the converse. Neither unstated clause is a distinct surviving theorem.
